Predict one human recipient's current choice in a resource allocation game. You interact through online chat with the same apparent other participant. You were led to believe your recipient role was randomly assigned. Earlier, in three dictator-game rounds, you had to receive3,1,0coins while the proposer kept7,9,10. A total of4coins for you versus26 for the proposer was announced; you then rated unfairness and emotions. There was no accept/reject decision in those dictator rounds.
Now the proposer allocates10coins in each ultimatum round. You can ACCEPT the current proposal, giving each player the proposed coins, or REJECT it, giving both players zero coins for that round. You were told to obtain as many coins as possible. Participation earns a gift voucher worth aboutUSD5, with a possible additional performance-based voucher worth aboutUSD10. The exact bonus criterion and any coin-to-currency conversion are not supplied here. Earlier own offers and choices below have already occurred; future offers and choices are not given. No advance knowledge of the total number of rounds is assumed.
Earlier ratings are your actual self-reports before this ultimatum game, on1..7scales. Emotion1 means not at all and7 a great deal; unfairness1 means not at all unfair and7 a great deal unfair. Baseline emotions were measured before the dictator game; after-dictator emotions and unfairness were measured after its three rounds, before this ultimatum game. Positive emotion ratings are expressed in their original direction. Age, gender, parental education and annual household-income bracket were collected in the follow-up survey; they describe your own stable, pre-existing characteristics, without inventing an exact income. Predict the recorded human choice, not an optimal or moral recommendation. Output only ACCEPT or REJECT.
